title: SuperSNEC: Fast and Accurate Supernova Light Curve Production Using Adaptive Gridding

creators.name: Fremling, Christoffer
creators.affiliation: California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, CA 91125, USA

creators.name: Hinds, K-Ryan
creators.affiliation: California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, CA 91125, USA

description:
SuperSNEC is a fast, open-source 1D Lagrangian radiation-hydrodynamics code for producing supernova bolometric light curves, designed for rapid generation of large model grids. It extends SNEC 1.01 (Morozova, Piro & Ott 2015) with runtime adaptive gridding of the computational grid, adaptive radioactive-heating cadence, optimized gamma-ray deposition and ray-tracing, flexible 56Ni mixing controls, and solver optimizations. At ~100 zones with adaptive gridding, SuperSNEC reproduces 1000-zone SNEC reference light curves to ~0.02 mag RMS while running ~400x faster (<2 seconds per model on a laptop CPU), enabling light-curve parameter inference over grids of ~106 models.

The repository contains the complete Fortran source, a ready-to-use parameter file, progenitor stellar profiles, and the Python analysis scripts and data needed to reproduce all tables and figures in the accompanying paper (Fremling & Hinds 2026, ApJ). Building requires only a Fortran compiler (e.g., gfortran) and a LAPACK library; compilation is a single 'make' command. See the README for usage instructions and a summary of all modifications relative to the original SNEC.

SuperSNEC is derived from SNEC 1.01 and, like the original code, is distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International license.
